focus: Section 2 (Distillation), softmax with temperature. Explain how the temperature T turns logits z_i into probabilities q_i. Let the learner edit a small vector of logits and the temperature. Show the scaled logits, the exponentials, the probabilities, and how soft the distribution is. Guide them through T=1 versus a high T and through equal logits. Check that probabilities sum to one, that equal logits give a uniform distribution at any T, and that the ordering of probabilities never changes with T.
audience: Engineering undergraduates who know what a neural-network classifier outputs.
excerpt: 2 Distillation (paraphrased). Neural networks usually produce class probabilities with a softmax output layer that converts the logit z_i computed for each class into a probability q_i by comparing z_i with the other logits: q_i = exp(z_i / T) / sum_j exp(z_j / T)  (Equation 1), where T is a temperature that is normally set to 1. Using a higher value of T produces a softer probability distribution over classes. In the simplest form of distillation, knowledge is transferred to the distilled model by training it on a transfer set using a soft target distribution for each case, produced by the cumbersome model with a high temperature in its softmax; the same high temperature is used when training the distilled model, and after training it uses a temperature of 1. Soft targets with high entropy carry much more information per training case than hard targets, because they reveal the relative probabilities of incorrect classes, for example that one wrong answer is far more likely than another.
